subject: Game Theory
title: Separation of Powers
description: A quick, practical guide to Separation of Powers.

hook.text: The US splits power among Congress, the President, and the courts. Why not let one body do everything?

buildup.text: Separation of powers creates multiple veto players, making it hard for any faction to seize total control.

discovery.text: In game theory, this is commitment through institutional design: leaders bind their own future power.

twist.text: The downside: gridlock. When branches disagree, government can't act—even when action is urgent.

climax.text: Parliamentary systems trade gridlock risk for efficiency: the executive and legislature are fused.

quiz.question: What is the game-theoretic purpose of separation of powers?
options: Preventing any faction from seizing total control
